q: How much CO2 does converting a foundry cupola to divided blast save?
title: Divided blast cupola: coke and CO2 saved
short: Roughly 75 t of CO2 a year in BEE's Batala, Jalandhar and Ludhiana report: fuel per 2.14 t melt drops from 500 kg to 400 kg, or 25 t over 250 melts. The report's own 25 t CO2 figure undercounts. Cost Rs 6.64 lakh, saving Rs 3.95 lakh a year, payback 1.68 years (2011).
audience: Grey iron foundry owners in Punjab and other cupola clusters deciding whether to rebuild a conventional cupola as a divided blast cupola

ul: One melt a day in an 8 to 10 hour shift, 250 days a year.
About 2.14 t of cast iron a melt at 1,300 to 1,500 C, taking 5 to 7 hours.
Fuel per melt falls from 500 kg to 400 kg, charge from 2.14 t to 2.10 t, and rejected metal from 140 kg to 100 kg.

sections.h: What a divided blast cupola changes
p: Blast air enters through two rows of tuyeres about a metre apart, split roughly equally, each row with its own wind belt so pressure and volume can be set separately.

Studies by BCIRA quoted in the report found 20 to 32% less charge coke and an 11 to 23% faster melt at the same tapping temperature. TERI's 1988 demonstration cupola in Howrah cut coke by 35% against a poorly designed divided blast unit.

sections.h: Why the report's 25 t CO2 is too low
p: The report saves 25 t of fuel a year and lists 25 t of CO2, though its own note gives 2.1 t of CO2 per tonne of fuel, which would be 52.5 t. It calls the fuel coal; cupolas burn foundry coke. At the IPCC default for coke, about 3.02 t of CO2 per tonne, 25 t of coke is about 75 t of CO2. If your invoices really show coal, use your coal's factor.

ul: Get the design worked out for your shell: tuyere area and number, the top to bottom air ratio, blower volume and pressure, well depth and stack height. A copied design loses most of the saving.
Weigh coke into every charge for a month before and after.
Track coke per tonne of good castings, not per tonne melted, so fewer rejects show up too.

example.title: 250 melts a year, before and after
lines: Before: 500 kg x 250 = 125 t coke x 3.02 = 377.5 t CO2
After: 400 kg x 250 = 100 t coke x 3.02 = 302 t CO2
Saved: 25 t coke, about 75.5 t CO2 a year
Per tonne melted: 500 / 2.14 = 234 kg coke (706 kg CO2) down to 400 / 2.10 = 190 kg (575 kg CO2)
example.note: Coke at the IPCC 2006 default, 107,000 kg CO2 per TJ at 28.2 GJ per tonne, an estimate. Blower power and limestone are left out.

senseible: Senseible reads coke and power invoices into monthly records with CO2 for each, so the change after a cupola rebuild shows up per tonne once you add your production. The green loan check tells you what a lender will ask for.
